title: Young Plants and Animals
seo_title: Grade 1 Young Plants and Animals Worksheets: Like Their Parents, But Not Exactly
standard_text: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
meta_desc: Free grade 1 science worksheets on young plants and animals (NGSS 1-LS3-1): how babies are like their parents but not exactly, matching babies to parents, and growing up. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Same kind and body parts. Different size, color or spots.
body_html:
How to think about it

Babies are like their parents, but not exactly.

  • Same: kind of animal, body parts.
  • Different: size, color, spots.
  • Tadpoles and caterpillars change as they grow.
Example

How is a puppy like its parent?

Look at the body parts.

Answer: four legs, fur and a tail

Example

How is a puppy different?

Look at size and color.

Answer: It is smaller and may be a different color.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking babies look exactly like their parents.
  • Thinking a kitten can grow into a dog.
  • Thinking a tadpole is a fish.

faq.q: How are young animals like their parents?
faq.a: They are the same kind of animal with the same body parts, like four legs, fur and a tail.
They are smaller, and they may have a different color, spots or stripes.

faq.q: Do all babies look like their parents at first?
faq.a: Not all. A tadpole and a caterpillar look different, but they grow up to look like a frog and a butterfly.
